records.name: Prefix-free incompressibility characterization of Martin-Löf randomness
records.statement: For an infinite binary sequence X, X is Martin-Löf random iff there is a constant c such that for every n, K(X↾n) ≥ n-c.

records.statement: Let (X,μ) be a computable probability space with no atoms. For x∈X, the following are equivalent: x is Schnorr random; x is T-typical for every mixing endomorphism T; and x is T-typical for every independent endomorphism T, with mixing/independence and T-typicality exactly as in DEF-0056/DEF-0057.

records.name: Equivalent computability criteria for probability measures

On Cantor space, μ is computable iff cylinder measures are uniformly computable.

records.name: V'yugin effective Birkhoff convergence for Martin-Löf-random sequences
records.statement: Let P be a computable probability measure on Cantor space, T a computable P-measure-preserving transformation, and f a computable real-valued function. Then the Birkhoff averages of f along T converge at every P-Martin-Löf-random sequence ω to an integrable T-invariant function \bar f(ω) with E_P(\bar f)=E_P(f). If T is ergodic, then \bar f(ω)=E_P(f) at every such random ω.
hypotheses: P is a computable Borel probability measure on infinite binary sequences
T is computable and preserves P
f is a computable real-valued observable
ω is Martin-Löf random with respect to P
ergodicity is required only for identifying the limit with E_P(f), not for convergence itself
records.direction: randomness implies pointwise Birkhoff convergence; ergodicity identifies the limit
cautions: The measure is an arbitrary computable Cantor-space probability measure, not silently fair coin.
Without ergodicity the theorem gives convergence to an invariant limit, not equality with the space expectation.

records.name: Effective Birkhoff theorem for effectively open and closed sets
records.statement: Let μ be a computable probability measure on Cantor space and T a computable a.e.-defined, μ-preserving, ergodic transformation. For every effectively open U and every μ-Martin-Löf-random ω, the averages n^{-1}Σ_{k<n} χ_U(T^kω) converge to μ(U); the same holds for effectively closed sets.
hypotheses: μ computable on Cantor space
T computable a.e.-defined, μ-preserving and ergodic
U effectively open (or effectively closed)
ω μ-Martin-Löf random
records.direction: randomness implies ergodic typicality for effective-set indicators

records.name: Effective Birkhoff theorem for lower semicomputable observables
records.statement: Under a computable probability measure μ on Cantor space and a computable a.e.-defined μ-preserving ergodic transformation T, if f:2^ω→[0,+∞] is lower semicomputable, then for every μ-Martin-Löf-random ω the Birkhoff average converges to ∫f dμ, with +∞ allowed.
hypotheses: μ computable on Cantor space
T computable a.e.-defined, μ-preserving and ergodic
f:2^ω→[0,+∞] lower semicomputable
ω μ-Martin-Löf random
records.direction: randomness implies effective ergodic theorem for lower semicomputable observables
cautions: Ergodicity is required for the integral value in this theorem.
The observable class is lower semicomputable and nonnegative as stated; do not replace it by an arbitrary L1 class by analogy.

hypotheses: (X,μ) computable probability space
T μ-layerwise computable, measure-preserving and ergodic
A effectively open with μ(A)<1
x μ-Martin-Löf random

records.name: Fair-coin Martin-Löf randomness characterized by nonergodic computable Birkhoff convergence
records.statement: On fair-coin Cantor space, a point x is Martin-Löf random exactly when it is weak Birkhoff for every computable measure-preserving transformation with respect to computable observables, using SRC-0058's transformation representation: the induced transformation is required to be defined and infinite outside a computable G_delta null set, not everywhere total. The positive convergence direction is the effective nonergodic theorem, and SRC-0058 proves the converse by constructing, for every non-Martin-Löf-random x, a computable measure-preserving transformation and a computable set whose indicator averages fail to converge at x.
hypotheses: ambient space is Cantor space with fair-coin/Lebesgue measure

transformations are computable and measure-preserving in SRC-0058's Cantor-space representation; the induced map is guaranteed defined/infinite outside a computable G_delta null set rather than on every input
observable class for the positive direction is computable; the converse witness is a computable set/indicator
no ergodicity assumption

records.name: Maximal constructive null-set characterization of Martin-Löf nonrandomness
records.statement: In the fair-coin setting of SRC-0001, the sequences nonrandom for a universal sequential test are exactly the intersection of its nested constructively open levels, and this nonrandom class is a maximal constructive null set: every constructive null set is contained in it.

records.name: Solovay-test characterization of Martin-Löf randomness
records.statement: In fair-coin Cantor space, an infinite binary real X is Martin-Löf random iff it avoids every Solovay test, where a Solovay test is a computable sequence (σ_i) of finite strings with bounded Σ_i2^{-|σ_i|}, and avoidance means that only finitely many σ_i are prefixes of X.
hypotheses: fair-coin Cantor space / binary expansion setting of SRC-0059
Solovay test as DEF-0061
cautions: The finite sum need not be a computable real. Adding computability of the total moves to the total-Solovay/Schnorr convention DEF-0017.
The inspected source explicitly attributes the result to Solovay, but the underlying Solovay draft remains uninspected; direct original-source priority is therefore not claimed here.

records.name: c.e.-martingale characterization of Martin-Löf randomness
records.statement: In the fair-coin Cantor-space setting of SRC-0059, an infinite binary real X is Martin-Löf random iff no c.e. martingale f succeeds on X, where c.e. means uniformly approximable from below and success means lim_n f(X↾n)=∞.
hypotheses: fair-coin Cantor space
f is a nonnegative martingale satisfying f(σ0)+f(σ1)=2f(σ)
f is c.e./uniformly lower semicomputable as in DEF-0062
cautions: This is not the computable-martingale characterization of computable randomness: the effective resource is lower semicomputability.
No arbitrary computable measure, supermartingale normal form or oracle-relativized version is inferred in P1-S011.
